text: Security is essential in web development. First, always use HTTPS to encrypt data between users and your server. Without it, attackers can steal passwords and personal information. Second, implement strong authentication, such as requiring complex passwords and two-factor verification. This helps confirm that users are who they claim to be. Third, validate all user input carefully. Never trust data from forms or URLs, because common vulnerabilities like SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS) often start there. Finally, stay informed about typical threats, including broken access control and insecure APIs. By following these basic practices, developers can build safer websites and protect both their users and their data.
